A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LaGoVAD method and PreVAD dataset. Their complete text, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable and support reliable matching across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: V2 reports original zero-shot detection and classification experiments, component and prompting ablations, and qualitative predictions in Section 6 and Appendix F.

after.justification: V3 retains those original experiments and adds an annotation-quality assessment in Appendix D.2 and prompt-failure experiments in Figure F.

M1.justification: The architecture, four training losses, inference procedure and dynamic synthesis Algorithm 1 remain equivalent. V3 adds explanations about mismatched descriptions, single-segment synthesis and retrieval features without establishing a change to the implemented procedure.

E1.justification: PreVAD training coverage and the seven detection test datasets are retained. V3 adds description-quality evaluation involving HIVAU-70K and tests ambiguous and contradictory user definitions on the existing trashcan video, extending the evaluated tasks and input conditions.

E2.justification: The detector and classifier comparator sets in Tables 2–4 are unchanged. The new annotation-quality comparison in Appendix D.2 evaluates constrained prompting against unconstrained prompting and uses HIVAU-70K descriptions as an additional quality comparator.

E3.justification: The new annotation study specifies 200 randomly sampled videos, three independent raters and a five-point scoring rubric in Table B. Figure F adds comparisons between good and problematic prompts. Existing training settings, test splits, metrics and drift@5 category subsets are unchanged.

E4.justification: V3 adds an assessment of whether category-constrained prompting improves annotation quality and illustrative failure analyses for contradictory and ambiguous definitions. The existing component, synthesis, data-usage and inference-prompt ablations are retained.

E5.justification: Appendix D.2 newly reports inter-rater reliability using ICC(2,k), with a value of 0.799. Existing drift@5 averaging is unchanged, and no additional training-seed information, confidence intervals or uncertainty estimates for detector performance are reported.

E6.justification: V3 adds mean annotation-quality ratings of 3.5 for unconstrained prompting, 4.3 for constrained prompting and 4.4 for HIVAU-70K, plus prompt-failure curves. Existing benchmark and ablation values are retained. Table 4 merely converts fractions to percentages, such as 0.857 to 85.7.

T1.justification: V2's informal deterministic-label hypothesis and probability decomposition are expanded into Assumption 1, two formal propositions and proofs in Appendix I. V3 establishes conditional invariance of P(Y|V,Z) under the assumption and specifies a sufficient probability-mass shift condition for concept drift in P(Y|V), substantially expanding the mathematical treatment.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same central claims: language-guided open-world detection, two regularizers, the 35,279-video PreVAD dataset and state-of-the-art zero-shot performance across seven datasets. The added evidence does not redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: V3 distinguishes theoretical drift avoidance from practical model performance. Appendices G.2 and H explain failure under contradictory prompts, attribute partial ambiguity robustness to CLIP, and discuss incorporating hidden external conditions into the anomaly definition. The earlier architecture limitations remain.

D1.justification: The abstract changes the code and dataset release from promised to reported as completed. Appendix D.1 specifies CC BY-NC 4.0 licensing, links and download scripts, and anonymized copies for unavailable videos. Table 4 newly identifies its VadCLIP comparator as PreVAD-trained. Core implementation settings remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V3 adds references to Cutout, VISTA, VERA and inter-rater reliability. Section 2.2 acknowledges MLLM methods' potential to address open-world problems through prompting while emphasizing limitations in systematic concept-drift evaluation and efficiency, and explicitly connects the regularizers to prior augmentation and contrastive-learning work.

P1.justification: V3 locally rewrites Section 3, refines related-work and method explanations, and reorders the ablation discussion. It adds assumption-discussion and proof appendices, an LLM-use declaration and acknowledgments, and updates publication headers. Most existing prose and the overall narrative structure are preserved.

P2.justification: V3 adds the scoring-rubric Table B and failure-case Figure F, enlarges existing displays such as Figures B and E, and relocates several figures and tables. Tables 3–4 gain clarifying captions, and Table 4 switches to percentage formatting. Existing visual evidence is otherwise retained.

improvement.justification: V3 makes the conditions behind drift invariance explicit, supplies quantitative evidence for previously asserted annotation quality, and exposes concrete prompt limitations. Clearer data-access and licensing information also improves transparency. These are useful gains in support and reproducibility; the additional robustness evidence remains illustrative, and the central method and benchmark findings are unchanged.
